headline: RBI issues Second Amendment to FEMA Export and Import of Goods and Services Regulations, 2026
summary_points: RBI has issued the FEMA (Export and Import of Goods and Services) (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2026.
An earlier amendment, notified on November 02, 2026, took effect retrospectively from October 01, 2026, based on stakeholder feedback.
RBI has also placed FAQs on the 2026 Regulations on its website to help exporters, importers and other stakeholders.
who_is_affected: Exporters, importers, Authorised Dealer banks and their advisers dealing with FEMA trade compliance.
action_required: Read the FAQs and the amendment regulations on the RBI website and align export-import documentation and AD bank processes accordingly.

RBI has issued the Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2026.

Background: the 2015 Export Regulations were superseded by the 2026 Regulations, issued on January 13, 2026 and effective from October 01, 2026. They are principle based and aim to ease doing business, especially for small exporters and importers, and to empower Authorised Dealers to serve customers faster.

Based on stakeholder feedback, Amendment Regulations were notified on November 02, 2026, with retrospective effect from October 01, 2026.

To help stakeholders understand the new trade regulations, RBI has also placed FAQs on its website.

Why it matters: exporters, importers and AD banks should review their processes against the amended regulations and the FAQs, particularly given the retrospective effect.

Please verify the details with the official RBI source before acting.
